full_description: A mover object A, a reference object B, and one distractor are on the table. The instruction tells the robot to pick up A and place it in a spatial DIRECTION relative to B: to the left of / to the right of / in front of / behind / on top of. Tests spatial-direction understanding: the SAME scene admits every direction, so the direction phrase alone decides the correct placement.
schema: {A} = the mover object (picked up), filled by play_once with the literal 'the {color} {noun}' (no '/', substituted verbatim). {B} = the reference object, same literal form. {D} = the direction phrase the instruction commands (a prepositional phrase: 'to the left of' / 'to the right of' / 'in front of' / 'behind' / 'on top of') -- it is the ONLY signal of the placement direction. {a} = arm. Every template MUST be exactly {A} {D} {B} (+ optional {a}), with {D} immediately before {B}. Do NOT write 'the' immediately before {A}/{B}/{a}; each already renders with a leading article. Color is a grounding aid, not a scored axis; the scored axis is the placement direction.
preference: One family for all five directions (the phrase is injected into {D}). num of words should not exceed 12. Keep {D} directly between {A} and {B}.
seen: Pick {A} up with {a} and place it {D} {B}
Use {a} to lift {A}, then set it {D} {B}
Use {a} to grab {A} and put it {D} {B}
Use {a} to pick {A} up and place it {D} {B}
unseen: Use {a} to grab {A} and place it {D} {B}
Use {a} to pick up {A}, set it {D} {B}
